easy.def: Wanting to do something very much.
examples: I am keen to learn to swim.
He is keen on trains.
She is a keen reader.

more.def: Very interested and eager; also, sharp or strong.
examples: Owls have keen eyesight for hunting at night.
The dog has a keen sense of smell.
He is a keen gardener who grows his own vegetables.

easy.def: To have something and not give it away.
examples: You can keep the book.
She keeps her toys here.
I kept the ticket.

more.def: To have something and not lose it or give it away, or to store it somewhere.
examples: You can keep the pencil, because I have another one.
We keep the flour in a jar in the cupboard.
He kept every card his friends gave him.

easy.def: To stay in the same way.
examples: Keep warm.
Please keep still.
She keeps smiling.

more.def: To stay in a certain state, or to continue doing something.
examples: A thick coat will keep you warm on the snowy hike.
The little bird kept singing all morning long.
Please keep quiet while the baby sleeps.

easy.def: A person who takes care of something.
examples: The zoo keeper fed the lions.
The keeper watched the sheep.
A goal keeper.

more.def: A person whose job is to look after or guard something.
examples: The zookeeper fed the lions.
The lighthouse keeper lit the lamp.
The goalkeeper blocked the shot.

easy.def: A small house or a place for dogs.
examples: The dog sleeps in the kennel.
A kennel in the yard.
We left our dog at the kennel.

more.def: A small shelter for a dog, or a place where dogs are kept and cared for.
examples: The dog slept in its kennel in the yard.
We left our dog at a kennel while we were on vacation.
The kennel has big runs for the dogs to play.
I put ketchup on my fries.
The ketchup is red.
Pass the ketchup.

more.def: A thick, red sauce made from tomatoes that is eaten with foods such as fries.
examples: I put ketchup on my burger.
The bottle of ketchup was empty.
He dipped his fries in ketchup.

easy.def: A pot with a spout for heating water.
examples: The kettle is hot.
Mom filled the kettle.
The kettle whistled.

more.def: A metal pot with a lid, a handle and a spout, used for boiling water for tea and other things.
examples: The kettle began to whistle as the water started to boil.
Grandpa filled the kettle and put it on the stove.
Steam poured out of the spout of the kettle.

easy.def: A small metal tool for opening a lock.
examples: I lost my house key.
The key opens the door.
Dad has the car key.

more.def: A small metal object that you turn to open or lock something.
examples: She turned the key and the door swung open.
Dad keeps the keys to the car on a hook.
The old chest had a small brass key.

easy.def: A button you press on a piano or computer.
examples: Press the key.
The piano has black keys.
I pressed a key on the computer.

more.def: One of the parts you press on a piano, a typewriter or a computer.
examples: He pressed each key on the piano and listened.
Press the space key to start the game.
The cat walked across the keys of the keyboard.
Practice is key.
A key idea is in the first line.
Teamwork is key for a good game.

more.def: Most important; needed in order to succeed.
examples: Sunlight is a key part of how plants make food.
The key idea in the story is friendship.
Practice is key if you want to get better at the piano.

easy.def: The keys you press on a computer or piano.
examples: I type on the keyboard.
She plays the keyboard.
The keyboard has many keys.

more.def: The set of keys that you press to type on a computer or to play music on a piano or an electronic instrument.
examples: I typed my story on the computer keyboard.
She played a tune on the keyboard in music class.
The piano keyboard has black and white keys.

easy.def: The hole in a lock where the key goes.
examples: He looked in the keyhole.
The key fits the keyhole.
The keyhole is small.

more.def: The hole in a lock where a key is put.
examples: She put the key into the keyhole and turned it.
A tiny keyhole in the old chest needed a small key.
He peeked through the keyhole of the door.
